```{r}
library(tidyverse)

```

## Rounding pi

```{r}
round(3.1415926)
round(3.1415926, digits = 2)
```

## Argument order

```{r}
print(seq(3, 10, 2))
```

## Variable type

```{r}
b = TRUE
print(paste(class(b), b))

c = 'variable'
print(paste(class(c), c))

```

## Data with radiated cells

```{r}
cell_ID_1 = 'CX1'
cell_ID_2 = 'CX2'
treated_1 = TRUE
treated_2 = FALSE
num_cells_before_1 = 5415
num_cells_before_2 = 8123
num_cells_after_1 = 1432
num_cells_after_2 = 7543
```

## Weird R behaviours

```{r}
print(TRUE + TRUE)
print(TRUE + FALSE)
print(5 + TRUE)
```

Boolean variables in R can behave like numbers.

## Fortune()

```{r}
fortune()
```

## Vectors

```{r}
vector <- c(10, 19, 100)

print(vector)
```

```{r}
cell_ID_1 = 'CX1'
cell_ID_2 = 'CX2'
treated_1 = TRUE
treated_2 = FALSE
num_cells_before_1 = 5415
num_cells_before_2 = 8123
num_cells_after_1 = 1432
num_cells_after_2 = 7543

cell_ID <- c(cell_ID_1, cell_ID_2)

print(cell_ID)
print(cell_ID[1])
```

```{r}
all_my_pets <- c("dog", "horse", "guinea pig", "chicken", "cat")

print(m <- all_my_pets[4])
```

```{r}
cell_colony_radius <- c(1, 3, 4, 2, 5, 8)
cell_colony_radius <- cell_colony_radius*2

print(cell_colony_radius)

# Vectorisation - arithmetic operations can be applied to a whole vector at once.
```

```{r}
ls <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 66)

(ls > 2)[1]
```

```{r}
data_frame_mine <- tibble(
  species = c('vampire bat', 'fruit bat', 'little brown bat'),
  diet = c('blood', 'fruit', 'fruit'),
  cuteness = c('no', 'amazing', 'meh')
)

gt(data_frame_mine)
```
